answer: Because the timing is recorded against the horizon challenge, the cipher audit can replay the wander history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 197 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A farm of 1826 identities would post 661 proofs and burn roughly 8 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
